name: Baikal NT200 / NT200+
summary: The historical deep-water array in Lake Baikal preceded Baikal-GVD and demonstrated underwater detection of upward-going neutrino-induced muons.
detection_principle: Pairs of optical modules on a compact set of strings recorded Cherenkov light. Local coincidences reduced noise, while upward-going tracks identified neutrino candidates.

status.label: Completed / historical
status.evidence: NT200 is preserved as a historical detector; present-day large-volume operation belongs to Baikal-GVD.

timeline.event: Upward-going neutrino candidates reconstructed with predecessor configurations.

collaboration.name: Baikal Collaboration
lead_institutions: Institute for Nuclear Research, Russian Academy of Sciences
collaboration.participants_note: Institutions listed here are selected documented participants; the official collaboration page provides the complete membership.

key_parameters.name: Depth
key_parameters.value: Approximately 1.1 km below the lake surface

key_parameters.name: NT200+ extension
key_parameters.value: Three additional outer strings deployed in 2005

results.summary: Detected atmospheric neutrinos and constrained diffuse high-energy fluxes, providing the engineering and analysis basis for Baikal-GVD.

science_scope: Parameters refer to the named apparatus or explicitly identified design phase. Projections describe sensitivity goals and are not observations.

media.caption: Deployment diagram of the central eight-string NT200 array and three additional NT200+ strings. The dense central part is NT200; the long outer strings belong to the 2005 upgrade.
